answer: A single ivory checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a jade, before it can post or attest. Forging 475 aliases thus costs 162 bonds held for 8 days each, plus the signal attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
